newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Banking Corp rehabilitation plan approved.
newsitem.headline: Manila Banking Corp rehabilitation plan approved.

text.p: The Monetary Board gave the go-ahead for the rehabilitation plan of Manila Banking Corp, a commercial bank controlled by the Puyat family which was closed and placed under receivership in 1987, the Central Bank said in a statement on Thursday.
The plan will involve the infusion within 30 days of 1.25 billion pesos in fresh capital from existing and new investors and the reypayment of debts within a year.

The bank has been given one year to comply with the terms and conditions of the rehabilitation plan before the Central Bank lifts its receivership and grants the authority to reopen for business, the statement said.

The investors include: the Vicente Puyat group which will bring in 375 million pesos; Andrew Tan Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc, 500 million pesos; Eusebio Tanco of Asian Terminals Inc, 250 million pesos; Antonio Tancaktiong of Jollibee Foods Corp, 120 million pesos; and Nelia Gonzales of Asiaworld Properties, 5 million pesos.

The shareholder composition will be as follows: Vicente Puyat group, 25.84 percent; Andrew Tan, 27.89 percent; Eusebio Tanco, 13.94 percent; Tony Tancaktiong, 6.69 percent; Nelia Gonzales, 0.28 percent; and the rest by other minority shareholders.
The new money will bring ManilaBank's capital to 3.884 billion pesos, the Central Bank said.
The debts to be paid in one year amount to 9.071 billion pesos and are owed to the board of liquidators of Central Bank and the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp.
These debts are to paid from existing liquid assets in the amount of 5.036 biilion pesos, collection from loans, sale of acquired assets and equity investments, the Central Bank said.
Interest charges incurred by the bank shall be paid in ten years, the Central Bank further said.
